Answer: A
Reason: The coronal CT image (Figure 3) demonstrates a soft tissue mass in the right paratracheal region at the level of the thoracic inlet (upper third), causing deviation of the trachea towards the left (patient's left, viewer's right). This extrinsic compression in the upper mediastinum can involve the recurrent laryngeal nerve or directly affect the larynx/trachea, explaining the patient's acute dysphonia. Although the option states "deviated towards the right," it is the only choice correctly identifying the location (upper third) and the mechanism (compression by an adjacent structure) consistent with the visible pathology and symptoms.
